questions.explanation:
LINE-BY-LINE WALKTHROUGH
`if 3 > 1:` — Selects behavior for a condition; without branches, different cases follow the same path.
`print('Condition is true')` — Runs an expression; print displays a value and calls may have side effects—without the line, that action does not occur.

questions.prompt:
What exact output does code example 2 in this lesson produce?

temperature = 18
if temperature < 20:
    print('bring a jacket')
questions.explanation:
LINE-BY-LINE WALKTHROUGH
`temperature = 18` — Binds the evaluated expression to a name; without the assignment, later lines cannot reuse that result.
`if temperature < 20:` — Selects behavior for a condition; without branches, different cases follow the same path.
`print('bring a jacket')` — Runs an expression; print displays a value and calls may have side effects—without the line, that action does not occur.

LINE-BY-LINE WALKTHROUGH
`for number in range(1, 4):` — Processes each iterable item; without the loop, remaining items are skipped.
`print(number * number)` — Runs an expression; print displays a value and calls may have side effects—without the line, that action does not occur.

questions.prompt: Which statement accurately describes “Syntax and indentation”?
options: Python is used for automation, web services, and data analysis because its readable syntax and broad library ecosystem make small, testable steps practical.
Comments explain a non-obvious decision instead of repeating the code, such as why a particular limit was chosen.
Syntax and indentation mark code-block boundaries; a mistake can prevent a route or condition from running.
Variables name and reuse values; aliases to a mutable list share the same object, so a change through one name is visible through the other.
questions.answer: Syntax and indentation mark code-block boundaries; a mistake can prevent a route or condition from running.
